attempts.evidence: Pass 1 — full 2000x2294 colour raster. Legend top-left carries exactly the manifest's two rows: red "premature — mistake · failing (runoff)", green "solved 34 km/h — ideal · good", and each line is stroked in its declared verdict colour (J1). Two hourglass turn points sit on the bottom straight, the red one visibly left of the green — the premature turn-in drawn where it happens; no ring or dot, which is what `marks: turn_point` asks for (J2). "premature turn point" leads to the red hourglass and "late apex — sight and exit" to a point on the green line inside the corner; both boxes are inside the frame and clear of other ink (J3). Two dashed rays run from the two eye positions to their limit points and the road beyond is washed darker, with the oncoming vehicle drawn where it blocks the view (J4). The red line turns in earlier, carries less lean, and terminates at the outer corridor edge captioned "ran off", with a hatched neutral ray continuing past it — the mistake reads as the mistake (J5). Diagram-mode disclosure does not apply in true mode (J6 na); no fan (J9 na).

Pass 2 — same raster, read for fabrication and for the new chrome. Every glyph traces to something declared: two lines, two turn points, two sight rays, one occluder, the legend, and the stage-8b/11 chrome the renderer owns (10/20/30/40 m ladder numbered on the ideal line only, entry stamps "34 km/h" on both lines, outcome words, the 5 m · 16 ft scale bar with "lane 3.5 m wide"). Nothing depicts an engine fact the envelope does not carry, and the consequence ray is hatched, arrowhead-free and neutral rather than verdict-coloured, so it cannot be read as a trajectory (J7). Both corridor edges are dotted inside the carriageway, and the red terminal sits on the carriageway edge as stage 8 claims (J1/J2 re-confirmed).

Pass 3 — greyscale conversion of the same raster, testing whether the verdict survives without hue. It does: the ideal line is the wider stroke and is captioned "clean" at its arrowhead, the mistake line is narrower and captioned "ran off" at its terminal, and the legend rows keep their words. Labels, ladder numbers and the scale bar all remain readable at this scale (J8).
